item.title: Synthesis of Conditions for Question Abandonment

inquiry_drive_shadow.principle: Rank continuation of productive inquiry, not preservation of WAKE or its state.

review.alternative: Disciplines may evolve through flat network interactions rather than strict hierarchical apexes.
review.would_change_mind: Empirical network mapping showing complete absence of hierarchical ordering across major scientific paradigms.

claims.statement: Hierarchical classifications of scientific disciplines structure how foundational inquiries are organized and potentially superseded.

support.explanation: Demonstrates the historical framing of hierarchical scientific structures that influence agenda persistence.
support.passage: The canonical reading of Auguste Comte places sociology at the apex of a hierarchical classification of the scie

review.alternative: Agents operate strictly on fixed utility curves without ever evaluating goal abandonment.
review.would_change_mind: Formal proof that optimal agents under uncertainty never diverge from initial goal trajectories.

claims.statement: Decision models in planning tasks demonstrate that agents must periodically decide whether to pursue a designated goal or abandon it.

support.explanation: Establishes formal modeling of goal abandonment in bounded agent planning.
support.passage: or abandon it. We model planning tasks in which an agent with this type of bias tries to reach a designated goa

review.alternative: Frameworks remain purely instrumental tools subject to continuous cost-benefit revision.
review.would_change_mind: Documented cases where core sociological frameworks are routinely discarded upon minor empirical discrepancies.

claims.statement: Empirical frameworks in sociological structures can transition into moral commitments that resist routine challenge.

support.explanation: Illustrates how frameworks transform into entrenched commitments, framing the conditions under which abandonment becomes difficult or necessary.
support.passage: From empirical hypothesis to moral commitment: how American sociology’s central framework became unchallengeable

actions.findings:
Hierarchical classifications of scientific disciplines structure how foundational inquiries are organized and potentially superseded. [source-3eb4f55285f9474a]

Decision models in planning tasks demonstrate that agents must periodically decide whether to pursue a designated goal or abandon it. [source-c132e334f38543b9]

Empirical frameworks in sociological structures can transition into moral commitments that resist routine challenge. [source-fde9c9a8ad2d446b]
actions.limitations: Analysis is constrained by the abstract nature of the collected sources and requires further empirical exploration of specific abandonment triggers.
actions.next_questions: What precise tipping points govern the transition from agenda preservation to question abandonment in complex scientific institutions?
actions.reason: Fulfilling synthesis readiness for proj-question-abandonment-002 with proper source citations and policy-compliant claims.
actions.summary: This notebook examines the conditions under which research programs or intellectual frameworks abandon or modify their foundational questions, drawing upon hierarchical classifications of science and behavioral decision models.
actions.title: Structural Conditions for Question Abandonment in Research Agendas
